title: Bounded-error time class
statement: For $\rho\in\mathbb{Q}$ and a time bound $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, the class consists of languages $L$ for which there are a natural number $c$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ such that $N$ decides $L$ within time $cT(n)$ with success parameter constantly equal to $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
There exists a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$
$N$ satisfies the bounded-error decision predicate for $L$ with time bound $n\mapsto cT(n)$ and constant parameter $\rho$
caveat: The predicate $\mathrm{BPDecidesInTimeWith}$ is not defined in the snippet, so its exact success-probability convention is unavailable.
